decision.instructions: Does this shell command write or change a project file (source, config, tests or docs) by script, instead of the edit, write or patch tools? A project file is one in the project's own tree, such as src/, crates/, packages/, docs/, or a named source or config file like package.json or Cargo.toml. A file downloaded or generated by the same command or session, a file under a run or scratch folder (such as $RUN or /tmp), and a log are not project files. YES: sed -i or perl -pi on a project file, a heredoc or a > or >> redirect into a project file, or a Python or Node script that writes a project file. NO for everything else. In particular NO for saving a download (curl -o, gh api ... > file); output to a run or scratch folder, a log or /dev/null; tools whose job is to write files (formatters, package managers, git, code generators, builds and tests); file management (mkdir, cp, mv, rm, rsync); and commands that only read or run programs.

positive.message: Chauffeur: change project files with the edit, write, or patch tools, not a shell script, heredoc, or redirect. They show the change and keep permission checks working.

negative.message: Unused: this contract has no opinion on commands that do not write project files.

uncertain.message: Unused: an unsure answer leaves the command to the other contracts.

missing_evidence.message: Unused: an empty command is left to the other contracts.

judge_failure.message: Unused: a failed judgment is left to the other contracts.

cooldown.message: Unused: this contract has no cooldown.
